stage: yoga arising (from the first stage on)
description: Seeing, hearing, thinking and knowing at a distance, omniscience, swiftness of mind, taking forms at will and acting without organs arise for the practitioner in whom yoga has arisen.

All become subject to him and he to none; he enters all and none enters him; he can slay all and none can slay him; he is fearless, imperishable, unaging, deathless and moves unobstructed everywhere (Kauṇḍinya: the eight marks of perfection).
Endowed with these qualities he becomes a great chief of Mahādeva's troops, surpassing all paśus in lordship.
After six months of constant yoga the powers arise in abundance - gradually, one after another, like a needle piercing a stack of lotus petals in succession.
Wandering alone as if mad, the ascetic is taken by others for a madman and a fool - the intended sign of the concealed stage.
The perfected yogin is not stained by action or by sin.
Dwelling in the cremation ground and living on what comes, he attains union with Rudra - direct conjunction with him (Kauṇḍinya).
Alone, secure, free from sorrow and vigilant, the mind wholly set on Rudra, he reaches the end of sufferings by the Lord's grace.
The Pāśupata siddhas at the Pāśupateśvara liṅga of Prabhāsa went to Śiva's abode in this very body (Purāṇic account).
Kapālakuṇḍalā arrives flying, saying she has drawn up the 'five nectars' through the rising order of the channels, having seen the self as Śiva in the heart-lotus - a hostile dramatist's portrayal.
The drunken Kāpālika declares that austerity gives the power to take any form - a satirist's portrayal.
